title: Update pytrilogy to 0.3.244, migrate to parse_engine_v2, bump extension to 0.1.32
body:
pytrilogy 0.3.244 ships a rewritten parser that replaces lark's `ParseTree`/`Token` + `ParseToObjects` with a new `SyntaxNode`/`SyntaxToken` AST and `TopLevelStatementParser`, and adds optional Rust (pest) backend support. All language server code is migrated to the new API.

## API migration

| Old | New |
|-----|-----|
| `trilogy.parsing.parse_engine.PARSER` | `trilogy.parsing.parse_engine_v2.parse_syntax` |
| `ParseToObjects` | `TopLevelStatementParser` |
| `lark.ParseTree` / `lark.Token` | `SyntaxNode` / `SyntaxToken` |
| `lark.UnexpectedToken` (incremental) | `InvalidSyntaxException` (single-shot) |

```python
# Before
parser = ParseToObjects(environment=env)
parser.set_text(text)
parser.prepare_parse()
parser.transform(PARSER.parse(text))
stmts = parser.run_second_parse_pass()

# After
doc = parse_syntax(text)
parser = TopLevelStatementParser(environment=env)
stmts = parser.parse(doc)
```

## Grammar structure changes

The new grammar unifies `datasource` and `root_datasource` into a single `datasource` node (root indicated by a `DATASOURCE_ROOT` token), restructures column lists as `column_assignment_list → column_assignment → concept_assignment → IDENTIFIER`, and places the table address under an `address` sub-node with an `ADDRESS` token. `extract_datasource_info` is updated accordingly.

## Error reporting

`error_reporting.py` no longer uses lark's incremental `on_error` callback. A single `try/except InvalidSyntaxException` block extracts line/column via a named regex constant (`_SYNTAX_ERROR_LOCATION_RE`) matched against the exception message.
